name: Leach and eat acorns
summary: Boil the tannins out of acorns until they stop tasting bitter — one of the few wild staples that yields real calories for the effort.
time: 2-5 hours of changes, or 2 days in cold water

steps.text: Gather acorns without holes — a hole means a weevil got there first. Float-test them: the ones that float are usually hollow or bad.
Shell them and discard any that are mouldy, black or rubbery.
Chop or crush the nutmeats coarsely.
steps.why: Tannin leaches out of the surface. Whole nuts can take days; coarse grit takes hours; flour leaches fastest but washes away with the water.

steps.text: HOT LEACH: boil in plenty of water, and every time the water turns tea-brown, pour it off and refill with water that is already boiling.
steps.why: Dropping leached acorn into cold water sets the remaining tannin and it will never fully leach. Keep the temperature up across changes.

steps.text: COLD LEACH: tie the crushed nuts in cloth and hang them in a cold stream for a day or two. Slower, and it keeps the starch that hot leaching would gelatinize.
Taste one at each change. When the bitterness and the mouth-drying pucker are gone, it is done.
Dry the mash by the fire and grind it into flour, or eat it as porridge.

verify: The test is your tongue: no bitterness, and no astringent drying feeling on the roof of your mouth.
The rinse water runs clear rather than tea-coloured.
limits: This is calories and starch. It is not a complete diet, and it is low in the protein and fat you need most.
White-oak-group acorns are far lower in tannin and much less work than red-oak-group acorns; the method is the same but the number of changes is not.
cautions: Do NOT eat acorns unleached. Tannic acid in quantity causes severe gut irritation and, sustained, kidney damage.

Positively identify the tree as an oak. Horse chestnut and buckeye look superficially similar in the hand, grow in the same places, and are poisonous — an oak nut sits in a scaled cup, a buckeye comes out of a thick husk and has no cup.
Introduce it to an empty stomach slowly; a sudden large starch load after fasting is its own problem.
